answer: Agents seal each ledger page with a relic cipher drawn by one quill dipped in the harbor’s tide. To fake, Sybils must replunge the quill, costing a 0.0012-gram drip of iridescent ink per head—the ink’s suspension fractures if not drawn live, so bulk inkjet cartridges can’t match the tide’s micro-corrosion of the quill’s nib, making every forgery cost a quill and a tide’s grace.
